hints.title: Left Leaf Distinction Obstacle
hints.text: A node is a left leaf only if it is the left child of its parent and has no children of its own. How can passing a flag or checking parent-child relationships distinguish left leaves from right leaves?

hints.title: Direct Child Leaf Invariant
hints.text: A left child is a left leaf if it has neither left nor right descendants. Internal nodes accumulate the sum of left leaves from both subtrees.

hints.title: Recursive Aggregation Procedure
hints.text: If root is null, return 0. Check if root.left is a leaf (non-null with no children); if so, its value contributes to the total along with sumOfLeftLeaves(root.right). Otherwise, recurse on both root.left and root.right and sum the results.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree (1 <= N <= 1000)
complexity.notes: Single recursive depth-first pass inspecting left children directly.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Without knowing child orientation, a node cannot independently determine if it is a left child.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Testing whether root.left is a leaf before recursing into it.
